Effects-engine tutorials — 9,170 real tutorials (one per catalog preset)

Every tutorial below drives the real OmniFrame effect engine: the property values are the exact engine patch the preset drops on a clip, and the steps are the app's universal workflow (Effects tab → drop/apply → FX Stack editing → ◆ keyframes → render). The count printed above is generated from the catalog at build time — nothing is padded. 12 tutorials carry rendered proof frames produced by the headless app renderer; 23 carry full step cards; the rest are indexed in the per-category recipe tables with their exact properties.

Glitch note: glitch techniques are EFFECTS now (intensity/style/scan/static/seed/rate, all keyframeable) — they left the transition picker in board J.

Full step-card tutorials (23)

Glitch Slice Heavyglitch

  1. Open the Effects tab (left dock) and pick the glitch sub-tab.
  2. Find Glitch Slice Heavy — drag its tile onto an image/video/compound clip (it tags the clip, full length, closed container) or click to apply; the L chip places it as an adjustment layer grading every track below.
  3. The inner cyan bar appears at the clip bottom: drag its body to move, the white end bars to trim (never leaves the parent; 0.1s minimum).
  4. Right panel → FX Stack: every property is an editable slider/select/colour — Glitch Intensity, Glitch Style, Scanlines, Static, Seed, Step Rate (Hz).
  5. Keyframe any numeric property: press ◆ at the playhead, move the playhead, change the value, press ◆ again (diamonds show on the timeline bar).
  6. Render/export — the effect lives only inside its bar range, stacks with any other dropped effects, and survives split (B) and trim.
glitch=0.75 · glitchStyle=slice · glitchScan=0.2 · glitchStatic=0.3 · glitchSeed=499 · glitchSpeed=12
Trace: glitchology taxonomy (transition pillars research) — now a keyframeable effect
